calls.head: Watch Calgary’s puck management
calls.body: Calgary gives up more dangerous chances after losing the puck than most (30th of 32 at avoiding breakdowns). Colorado ranks 3rd for chances off turnovers.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: 3.3% of Colorado’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against its usual 7.7%.

calls.head: Expect Colorado to fire from everywhere
calls.body: Few teams shoot as often as Colorado: 69.6 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5, 1st in the league. Calgary sits 27th of 32 at keeping shots down.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: Colorado took 74.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against its usual 69.6.

calls.head: Expect a track meet
calls.body: Colorado’s games average 88.6 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (1st of 32 for pace); Calgary’s average 85.3 (3rd).
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 97.4 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the two teams’ usual 87.0 and a league average of 82.0.

CGY.head: We gave Calgary only a 34% chance, and it went the way we feared.

COL.head: We gave Colorado a 66% chance, and Colorado delivered.

surprises.head: Colorado tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Lehkonen, N. Kadri, N. MacKinnon played 12:08 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Colorado’s usual lines.

surprises.head: Calgary tried a different line
surprises.body: J. Farabee, M. Backlund, Y. Sharangovich played 11:51 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Calgary’s usual lines.
